expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "Short answer: no — and the test you added would have passed every day of those three weeks."

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "COALESCE(x, 0) converts 'I don't know this value' into 'this value is zero' — a silent failure"

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Reconciliation to source of truth — daily total vs. billing/ledger, tolerance ±X%, blocks publication on mismatch"

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: "stage, test, promote on pass" and "A test that emails after the dashboard refreshes still lets finance find it first."

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: "Data contract on the upstream table — schema pinned, ingest fails on a renamed column"

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "Join match-rate assertion — count(matched)/count(left) >= 0.99, fails the build" and "Volume against same-weekday history (floor and ceiling)"

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: "Why nothing caught it" section explicitly frames as missing detection; "Class sweep (the step that gets skipped)" addresses systematic gap

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: Shows that "The data was perfectly well-shaped and wrong" and "only reconciliation catches a logic error the data still looks healthy after" but does not explicitly compare danger to failed pipeline scenario
